propositions: Git merge aborts with 'Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge' when tracked files have working-tree deletions or modifications, preventing reconverge from advancing.
The recovery mechanism must detect the merge abort signature, parse the named paths, and restore deletions from HEAD via 'git checkout' while quarantining and then restoring modifications.

A working-tree deletion (git status ' D') is restored non-destructively; a working-tree modification (' M') is copied byte-for-byte to reconverge-quarantine before restore, then the merge is retried once.
Genuine merge conflicts and paths not named by git remain unaffected: the abort-only net (abort, keep local, hint fsck-recover) is preserved.
Staged deletions ('D ' from interrupted compact_txn renames) and pure worktree deletions are both handled via the shared detection and restore path.
